mission: The squeeze lands on Ben and Talon within hours. They return to Iressa's secondary cache to find it raided and burned — no bodies, no witnesses, the documentary reconstruction professionally unrecoverable. The professionalism is the threat: someone told Greyline where the cache was, and the breach point is unknown. A warrant goes out for Talon on a planted Coruscant crime; Talon reads Tess's tradecraft fingerprint in one sentence and goes cold rather than hot. With every alternative closed, they relocate to the Skywalker family apartment — the one address neither of them has ever connected to an operation. From there, Ben holo-calls Luke at Shedu Maad. Brief. Ben tells him what has happened. Luke does not tell Ben to come to Shedu Maad. He does not tell him to go to Iresh. He says he understands and he will do what he can from where he is. The conversation ends with Luke knowing what Ben has just decided.
why_now: Korda becoming visible forced Tess’s hand. Ben and Talon’s operational capability, confirmed by the Korda chase, means Tess has to close all their alternatives now — before they can build a case that survives Ben’s absence. Three moves in a few hours: Korda’s death and the public fall-guy narrative, the cache raid that destroys Ben’s documentary reconstruction, and Talon’s frame that ends Luke’s quiet legal cover. Each move by itself is bad. Together they leave one door open.
conflict: Every door except Iresh is being closed by someone who closes doors for a living. Ben and Talon's conflict is with an absence: no enemy in the room, just burned evidence, a planted warrant, and the professional certainty that the next move was priced before they made it.
turning_point: Ben and Talon, hiding in the Skywalker family apartment, begin preparing the off-grid transit to Iresh.
closing_hook: Ben and Talon, hiding in the Skywalker family apartment, begin preparing the off-grid transit to Iresh.
setting: Two locations. (A) Iressa's secondary cache in the warehouse district — raided and burned: slagged terminals, ash where the documentary reconstruction was, the smell of accelerant used precisely. (B) The Skywalker family apartment, after dark — go-bags on the table, the family holo unlit, the secure terminal's glow the only light while Ben makes the call he has been avoiding.
emotional_trajectory: Tess should feel terrifying because he is calm and operational. He does not rage, he does not gloat, he just clears the board. The cache raid should land through absence rather than action — Ben and Talon walk into a destroyed space, no enemy present, only the evidence of professionalism. The frame should make Talon go cold, not hot. The Luke call should be the quietest beat in the chapter, and the most painful. Reader-onboarding / clarity note: Plain-language consequence: the bad guys just closed every option Ben had except the most dangerous one. They did it surgically. They did it because Ben is involved. The clock is no longer theoretical. Craft notes: - The cache raid happens off-screen for Ben. He arrives after. The reader experiences the loss through the destroyed space. - Who told Greyline where the cache was stays unanswered. The drafter should plant the question without resolving it. - Tess’s tradecraft fingerprint on the frame should be quiet, not declamatory. Talon notices, gives one small reaction, names it in a sentence when Ben asks.

stakes.personal: Ben walks into the burned cache and sees the ash where the documentary reconstruction was. Whatever case he was building for Saba is gone. He is no longer in the position of a Jedi Knight making a careful institutional argument — he is hunted, legally compromised, and out of official options.
stakes.interpersonal: The Talon frame is Tess's tradecraft fingerprint: specific construction patterns, a particular routing of planted evidence. Talon recognizes it in one sentence and goes cold. The valve doesn't shut — it freezes. Tess knows exactly how Talon thinks. That's the worst part. The second Luke call from the apartment is short, quiet, and ends without resolution — Luke understands what Ben has decided and doesn't try to stop him.
stakes.external: Three beats compound: (1) Korda is dead, shaped as a fall-guy narrative — rogue security director, no Foundation culpability. (2) The cache is professionally destroyed — no documentary case survives. (3) Talon is framed for a current Coruscant crime — Luke's quiet legal cover is ended. Simultaneously, Greyline's Iresh staging has accelerated past the timeline Ben captured from Korda. Every door is closed except the most dangerous one.

sensory_details: Tess's office: durasteel desk, single visitor chair, no personal effects, forty-second floor — the view from here is other buildings' climate exhaust. Clean and anonymous, the kind of space designed to carry no forensic weight. Iressa's cache after the raid: slagged terminals, ash where her labeled crates of datachips were, the smell of burning plastoid that hasn't fully cleared. The Skywalker apartment at night: familiar recycled air, the family holo still on the shelf — the same room, very different weight now.
canon_elements_needed: Shedu Maad / Hapes Jedi HQ continuity
Iresh physical geography and local survival rules

turning_point_detail.trigger: From the Skywalker apartment, Ben holo-calls Luke. Brief. Ben tells him what has happened — cache burned, Talon framed, Iresh already moving. Luke does not tell Ben to come to Shedu Maad. He does not tell him to go to Iresh.
turning_point_detail.shift: Luke says he understands and he will do what he can from where he is. The call ends with Luke knowing what Ben has decided. Neither of them says it.
turning_point_detail.cost: The apartment has become their final refuge. They begin preparing the off-grid transit to Iresh. The question of who told Greyline where the cache was is planted and unanswered.

emotional_arc.start: Tess POV opens: operational, calm, cleaning the board. No gloating. Korda's death is logistics.
emotional_arc.shift: Ben and Talon arrive at the burned cache. The absence is the threat — no enemy, no bodies, just the evidence of what professionalism leaves behind. Talon reads the Tess tradecraft fingerprint on the frame and goes cold.
emotional_arc.end: The Luke call from the apartment: the quietest beat in the chapter, and the most painful. Ben and Talon begin preparing for Iresh. They have nowhere else to go.

key_beats.beat_description: Ben and Talon arrive at Iressa's secondary cache to find it raided and professionally destroyed — slagged terminals, ash where the documentary reconstruction was.
key_beats.state_change: The case Ben was building for Saba is gone; the breach point is unidentifiable; who told Greyline where the cache was is unanswered.
key_beats.pov_reaction: The read of the room happening before the meaning of it does — the stillness of someone taking inventory of a loss.

key_beats.beat_description: A warrant goes out for Talon on a planted Coruscant crime; Talon reads Tess's tradecraft fingerprint in one sentence and goes cold rather than hot.
key_beats.state_change: Talon's legal cover is ended, Luke's quiet institutional protection is nullified, and Iresh staging has already accelerated past the timeline captured from Korda.
key_beats.pov_reaction: The valve freezing rather than shutting — watching Talon go still and knowing that is the worst version of his reaction.

key_beats.beat_description: Ben and Talon relocate to the Skywalker family apartment — the one address neither of them has ever connected to an operation.
key_beats.state_change: The apartment becomes their final refuge; the second visit lands with very different weight than the first.
key_beats.pov_reaction: The family holo still on the shelf — noted, not approached — and the specific quality of a room that hasn't changed while everything around it has.

key_beats.beat_description: From the apartment, Ben holo-calls Luke — brief, quiet; Luke understands what Ben has decided and does not try to stop him; the call ends without resolution.
key_beats.state_change: The second Luke call marks the point of no return: Luke knows, and his not-stopping is itself a form of permission.
key_beats.pov_reaction: The silence after the call ending — not relief, the thing after a door closes that was always going to close.
